title: PWHL fans in Toronto more receptive to brand sponsorship than Montreal
Sesame becomes the new Main Sponsor of Levante UD
article_text:
The leading comprehensive platform in talent and human resources management supports the club for the entire season.

Levante UD and Sesame, the leading comprehensive platform for talent and human resources management, have reached a sponsorship agreement through which the Valencian technology company becomes the Main Sponsor of the club starting from the 2026/27 season.

As the main sponsor of the men's first team, Sesame will feature on the front of the official game jersey as we already saw a few days ago with the launch of the first and second kits, on training gear, and on other physical and digital assets of the club. The agreement also includes a comprehensive program of activations, VIP experiences, corporate events, and content initiatives that will bring the brand closer to fans and the business community.

For Sesame, this sponsorship represents a key step in its brand positioning and visibility, associating itself with one of the historic clubs of Spanish football and a benchmark in Valencian sports. Additionally, this agreement reflects a growing trend in which high-growth technology companies seek to connect their brands with spaces capable of generating community, belonging, and shared emotions. For the company, football represents an environment where values such as teamwork, perseverance, and talent development are experienced every day.

“This alliance with Levante UD makes perfect sense for us. Football and scale-ups like Sesame have much more in common than it seems. Both of us thrive on building teams, developing talent, making quick decisions, and competing every day to improve. At Sesame, we believe that this way of understanding growth deserves to go beyond offices and connect with millions of people,” stated Albert Soriano, CEO of Sesame.

The head of Sesame also emphasized the local nature of the collaboration. “We are especially excited that this agreement is with a club from our homeland. We are a tech company born in Valencia that now works with companies all over the world, and we are very proud of our origins as well as being able to support Levante UD,” added Soriano.

For Levante UD, it is a great satisfaction to be associated with and display on their chest the brand of a Valencian technology company that is a leader in the field of human resources. “The arrival of Sesame as the main sponsor reinforces our commitment to innovation, professionalism, and continuing to grow hand in hand with companies that are transforming their sectors from Valencia to the world,” stated Pablo Sánchez, president of Levante UD.

Following the announcement of this agreement, Sesame and Levante UD are opening a new phase of collaboration in which various joint actions are planned, as well as the promotion of projects that go beyond sports sponsorship, bringing innovation, technology, sports, and the values of talent closer to Levante fans and society as a whole.

Sesame is human resources software focused on redefining the employee experience. It allows the digitalization of the most routine human resources processes so that managers and HR professionals can focus on talent, professional development, and the well-being of their teams, thereby growing their business and building a successful corporate culture. Currently, they have more than 20,000 clients in over 30 countries across Europe and Latin America.

title: Bodø/Glimt lead global football clubs with 555 per cent social media growth in 2026
article_text:
Bodø/Glimt recorded the highest percentage increase in social media followers among the world’s leading football clubs in 2026, with their combined Instagram and TikTok audience increasing by 555 per cent between 1st January and 17th November, according to data platform Football Benchmark.

The club’s following grew from approximately 136,000 to 888,000, placing them at the top of Football Benchmark’s ranking of the ten fastest-growing clubs by percentage. Their 555 per cent growth rate was more than 2.7 times that of Chicago Fire FC, the second-ranked club, which recorded an increase of 205 per cent, with Turkish side Trabzonspor registering 140 per cent growth closing in the first three clubs with the biggest digital increase. Also worth highlighting is the contrast with Como 1907, the emerging force in Italian football, which ranked fourth with 138 per cent growth – more than five times lower than Bodø/Glimt’s figure. The analysis took into account only clubs with at least 100k total followers across Instagram and TikTok.

Having competed in Norway’s second division as recently as 2017, Bodø/Glimt have transformed their sporting standing through sustained development and consistent performances on the European stage. Last season’s Uefa Champions League campaign, featuring victories over Manchester City and Atlético de Madrid before eliminating Inter, further elevated the club’s international profile.

The figures demonstrate how sporting performance and European competition exposure can accelerate international audience growth, creating opportunities to strengthen brand positioning, expand commercial reach and attract new partners.

Bodø/Glimt’s achievement also highlights the changing dynamics of football’s global attention economy, where ambitious clubs can build significant international audiences through sporting credibility and a distinctive competitive identity, challenging the traditional dominance of established football brands.

Source: Football Benchmark Social Media Analytics Platform. Combined Instagram and TikTok followers, 1 January–17 November 2026.

title: F1 Qatar GP: Antonelli leads Russell in opening practice
article_text:
Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli has comfortably topped first practice at Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix, holding off Mercedes team-mate George Russell as drivers grappled with the tricky Lusail circuit.

One week on from the high-speed drag race on the streets of Las Vegas, drivers and teams were facing a completely different challenge as they sampled the high downforce motorcycle track of Lusail.

In the opening stages of the first hour of practice on the smooth swoops of the Doha track, they deployed both Pirelli's medium and hard tyre compounds to get the lay of the land and gather data.

This year's world champion Antonelli led all the way through, setting an early benchmark of 1m24.057s on mediums and then gradually chipping away on subsequent run, establishing a 1m23.217s lap after 20-odd minutes to head Mercedes team-mate Russell by seven tenths.

The Mercedes pair led the cars of Red Bull, McLaren and Ferrari as they populated the leaderboard two by two, until teams started switching to the soft-tyre compound at the halfway point.

But despite deploying the softer and faster tyre compounds, Antonelli's early benchmark proved tough to topple. Russell, who was experimenting with different wing configurations, came short by half a second, while Antonelli also couldn't touch his own medium-tyre lap as the Lusail surface became littered with gravel from the many off-track excursions.

In the Red Bull Isack Hadjar set third, 0.661 in arrears, followed by a nervous looking pair of McLaren cars in the hands of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, who both conceded eight tenths, and Las Vegas winner Max Verstappen.

Ferrari was the fourth-fastest team after a muted session, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton over 1.2s adrift from Antonelli after grappling with massive front tyre degradation.

Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad led the midfield aboard the VCARB 03, with Alpine's Pierre Gasly rounding out the top 10.

title: The Inside Story on the Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team’s Triumphant Season
article_text:
Last week, motorsport’s controlled maelstrom that is Formula 1 descended on Las Vegas for the 21st grand prix of the 2026 season. Yet the biggest questions, namely, who would secure the Constructors’ crown and the Drivers’ Championship title had already been answered by the Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 team and its young phenom Kimi Antonelli, respectively.

Prior to Friday’s qualifying session, Bradley Lord, deputy team principal for the Mercedes squad, visited our House of Robb Las Vegas Grand Prix pop-up, located at the Allē Lounge on the 66th Floor of Resorts World. There, the second-in-command under Toto Wolff discussed why success came so decisively this season and shared insights on the team’s drivers, the tactical approach for the remainder of the season, and how the world’s premier race series has become a thriving business.

“It’s completely transformed in the last decade, from a niche sport of enthusiasts racing around the world to, you know, one of the biggest and fastest growing sports in the world, with a vastly different footprint, vastly different profile, and with that, the revenue that we’re able to generate as a team has expanded enormously,” Lord told the audience. “This year, we should hit $1 billion in revenue for the very first time, which is quite amazing for a small manufacturing company in the middle of the U.K.,” he mentioned regarding the team’s financial renaissance.

More impressive than the recent fiscal performance of Mercedes, though, has been its dominance in Formula 1 since 2014, when it began a winning streak of Constructors’ Championship titles that continued through 2021. Not only was that a legacy-defining span for the team, but also for its star driver Lewis Hamilton, who finished first in the Drivers’ Championship six of those seasons, bringing his total—so far—to seven.

The past four years have been decidedly more challenging for the Silver Arrows, especially with the series swapping to ground-effect cars, leaving Red Bull Racing and McLaren taking turns at the top. In 2025, Mercedes won only two races, while George Russell and Kimi Antonelli ended the season in fourth and seventh, respectively. This season, Antonelli had earned enough points by the end of the Mexico City Grand Prix to be crowned the overall victor, and Mercedes—winning 12 races—was the undisputed Constructors’ Champion after the contest in Brazil on November 8. So, what changed?

“Periodically in Formula 1, every sort of four five years, we have a major rules change . . . usually designed to slow the cars down, because every year they get faster, and at some point they get unsafe for the circuits we race on,” explained Lord. “And for 2026, we changed both the power units, so changed the engines—still 1.6-liter V-6 turbos, but with much more electrical energy as part of the overall power, so we’ve got over 1000 hp. Roughly 50 percent of that comes from an electric motor, 50 percent of it from the combustion engine; and around that new power unit, we put new aerodynamic regulations.” According to Lord, adapting to the new protocols also necessitated that the chassis, electronic control unit, and tires were all new as well.

The herculean course change for the cars also required reimagining what would feed the internal-combustion engines in order to complement the environmental ethos of hybridization. “Developing an advanced sustainable fuel means also developing all the infrastructure to produce that fuel as well. So that’s been an enormous job,” said Lord. “So we did the opposite of what you were always taught in chemistry or in physics at school, which is, if you do an experiment, change one thing at a time. We ripped up everything at the same time and landed with a new formula for 2026.” Of the shift in parameters dictated by Formula 1, Lord summed up the obvious by noting; “We have done a better job than the other teams in navigating that rule set.”

The transformation of Kimi Antonelli, who landed on the team’s radar when he was only around 11 years old (such was his karting prowess), has been more compelling to witness. Selected to fill the seat Hamilton vacated to join Ferrari, Antonelli had a rookie year that more than hinted at his potential, but few could have anticipated what would follow.

“It seems crazy to think that Kimi only won his first race, and got his first pole position, in China this year at the second race of the season,” said Lord. “From there, he went on a run of wins . . . five in a row that set himself up for an unexpected but quite remarkable championship challenge—he’s done all that at the age of 20, and so he’s become the first Italian champion in 73 years.” Equally noteworthy for Lord is how the young driver has handled it all. “He’s managed to both deliver something very, very exceptional, but also keep his feet on the ground and stay incredibly humble, grounded, and in touch with reality at the same time.”

His teammate George Russell’s experience, despite winning the Australian Grand Prix in March to start it all off, has been markedly different. “George has had both the strongest and the most disappointing season of his career,” mentioned Lord. “He’s had the lion’s share of the technical problems we’ve had. We’ve had a lot of unreliability in this first season with the new cars and the new engines, and he has struggled with that more than Kimi . . . he’s had a season that’s really tested his resilience.”

title: Tickford Racing strikes significant sponsorship extension
article_text:
Castrol considered its relationship with Tickford among its most successful with 92 race wins and is the second in its motorsport sponsorship portfolio alongside M-Sport.

Castrol first partnered with the Supercars heavyweights in 2003 under the Ford Performance Racing banner, through the Prodrive period and into the Tickford era.

‍”We’re thrilled to announce the extension of the Castrol-Tickford partnership into Year 25 and beyond,” said Castrol Australia and New Zealand head of marketing Jotika Prasad.

“Castrol’s commitment to Australian motorsport is a vital part of our DNA, and Castrol’s partnership with Tickford is certainly a key element of that.

“Castrol’s global association with Ford and Ford Racing programs is something we’re very proud of, and it’s certainly special that one of our longest-standing motorsport associations is right here in Australia.”

Tickford Racing will go into 2027 with an unchanged driver line-up of Cameron Waters and Thomas Randle.

Since graduating from the Super2 Series to Supercars, Randle has carried Castrol’s colours on his cars.

“It’s fantastic to announce that Castrol has re-signed with Tickford Racing for 2027 and beyond,” Randle said.

“I’m super pumped to continue our amazing partnership, a deal that has been going for 25 years.

“It just shows incredible loyalty between Tickford Racing and Castrol and I know that it’s a partnership that is valued.

“Castrol has been my number one supporter for many years now – not only in Supercars but also through my junior ranks.

“We’ve done some amazing things together, whether at the track or off it, I just can’t wait to see what’s in store for 2027 and beyond.”

Tickford Racing chief executive officer Simon Brookhouse hailed the long-standing relationship between his team and Castrol.

‍”We are incredibly proud to continue our longstanding partnership with Castrol,” said Brookhouse.‍

“The Castrol brand is integral to who we are as a race team and without their loyal support we would not be in the position we are in today.

“Castrol’s support and passion for what we do is amazing and it allows us to continue to push boundaries within the race team.

“It goes without saying, but to be one of Castrol’s longest standing partnerships globally is something we do not take for granted and we are excited to continue with them into the future.”
